new_jobs.title: Institutional Biosafety Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

Job Description

We have an opening for an Institutional Biosafety Program Manager
to provide strategic and technical leadership for LLNL’s institutional biosafety program. In this role, you will manage the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of a comprehensive biosafety program supporting biological research, laboratory animal research, and related institutional review activities.

You will work closely with Environment, Safety and Health leadership, principal investigators, research teams, institutional committees, and the Department of Energy to ensure that biological research is conducted safely, securely, and in compliance with applicable federal, state, local, and Laboratory requirements.

This position is in the Occupational Safety, Health and Environmental Protection Department within the Environment, Safety and Health Directorate.

This position offers a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. The ability to work from home one or more days per week may be available after a probationary period.

You will

Manage and continuously improve LLNL’s institutional biosafety program, policies, procedures, and program documentation.
Provide expert technical guidance on biosafety, biosecurity, biological research risks, containment concepts, and laboratory operations.
Develop program strategies, priorities, performance objectives, and resource requirements aligned with Laboratory mission needs.
Lead risk assessments for new and ongoing biological research activities and support development of Biological Use Authorizations.
Oversee biosafety reviews involving biological agents and materials, including activities conducted at BSL-1 through BSL-3 and ABSL-1 through ABSL-3 containment levels.
Ensure compliance with applicable requirements and industry standards, including Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories, NIH Guidelines, OSHA standards, DOE requirements, and other applicable federal, state and local regulations.
Serve as the Institutional Biosafety Officer and participate as a voting member of the Institutional Biosafety Committee, Biological Review Committee, Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee and Institutional Review Entity.
Serve as an institutional technical liaison with DOE, the DOE Livermore Field Office, USDA, and other regulatory or oversight organizations.
Oversee biosafety audits, inspections, assessments, investigations, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
Develop and maintain emergency response procedures for incidents involving biological agents and materials.
Oversee institutional biosafety training, including curriculum development, regulatory updates, delivery, and compliance tracking.
Establish and maintain data-driven performance measures, leading indicators, and program health metrics.
Compile, analyze, and communicate biosafety program information for leadership, oversight bodies, committees, and regulatory agencies.
Provide biosafety input into the planning, renovation, and design of biological research facilities.
Build collaborative relationships with principal investigators, researchers, line managers, staff, committees, and external stakeholders.
Benchmark biosafety practices with other DOE laboratories and research institutions.
Lead, mentor, and develop biosafety professionals and other program personnel, as assigned.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship.
Masters degree in biology, microbiology, molecular biology, virology, immunology, or a related life sciences field, or an equivalent combination of education and substantial relevant experience.
Extensive experience managing or leading institutional biosafety programs in a research laboratory, biotechnology, government, or comparable environment.
Expert knowledge of biosafety principles, laboratory operations, pathogenic microbiological techniques, biological containment, and biological hazard controls.
Expert knowledge of applicable biosafety regulations, standards, and guidelines, including BMBL, NIH Guidelines, OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens requirements, and relevant DOE requirements.
Substantial experience with biosafety or voting membership in relevant biogovernance committees such as IBC, IRE, IACUC, or equivalent committees.
Demonstrated experience conducting or overseeing biological research risk assessments, laboratory inspections, audits, incident investigations, and corrective action programs.
Experience developing policies, procedures, training programs, performance measures, reports, and other institutional program documents.
Demonstrated ability to interpret highly complex or ambiguous regulatory requirements and apply them across diverse research and operational environments.
Experience managing resources, projects, priorities, budgets, or personnel within a complex organization.
Excellent communication, facilitation, collaboration, negotiation, presentation, and conflict-resolution skills.
Strong analytical, organizational, situational awareness, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Demonstrated ability to build trust, gain consensus, and influence personnel at all levels while maintaining high standards of safety and compliance.

Qualifications We Desire

Current certification or registration through the American Biological Safety Association, such as Certified Biological Safety Professional or Registered Biosafety Professional.
Experience working at the BSL-3 or ABSL-3 containment level.
Knowledge of CDC and USDA import, export, transport, and permit requirements.
Experience with biological security, biosecurity, or biological risk management.
Experience with DOE directives, orders, laboratory operating contracts, or other federal research requirements.
Experience supporting the design, commissioning, or renovation of biological research facilities.
Experience developing data-driven program metrics and communicating program performance to senior leadership.
Experience supervising, mentoring, recruiting, or developing biosafety professionals.
Experience leading biosafety programs in a national laboratory or other highly regulated research environment.

Pay Range:
$240,960- $305,544 Annually

This is the lowest to highest salary range in good faith we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Additional Information

Position Information

This is a Career Indefinite position, open to Lab employees and external candidates.

Why Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory?

Included in 2026 Best Places to Work by Glassdoor!
Flexible Benefits Package
401(k)
Relocation Assistance
Education Reimbursement Program
Flexible schedules (*depending on project needs)
Our values - visit https://www.llnl.gov/inclusion/our-values

Security Clearance

This position requires a Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance. If you are selected, we will initiate a Federal background investigation to determine if you meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information or matter. Also, all L or Q cleared employees are subject to random drug testing. Q-level clearance requires U.S. citizenship.

Pre-Employment Drug Test

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. This includes, but not limited to cell phones, tablets, fitness devices, wireless headphones, and other Bluetooth/wireless enabled devices.

If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.

How To Identify Fake Job Advertisements

Please be aware of recruitment scams where people or entities are misusing the name of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) to post fake job advertisements. LLNL never extends an offer without a personal interview and will never charge a fee for joining our company. All current job openings are displayed on the Career Page under “Find Your Job” of our website. If you have encountered a job posting or have been approached with a job offer that you suspect may be fraudulent, we strongly recommend you do not respond.

To learn more about recruitment scams: https://www.llnl.gov/sites/www/files/2023-05/LLNL-Job-Fraud-Statement-Updated-4.26.23.pdf

Equal Employment Opportunity

We are an equal opportunity employer that is committed to providing all with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, marital status, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, protected veteran status, age, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws.

Reasonable Accommodation

Our goal is to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates applying and interviewing at the Laboratory. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please use our online form to submit a request.

California Privacy Notice

The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) grants privacy rights to all California residents. The law also entitles job applicants, employees, and non-employee workers to be notified of what personal information LLNL collects and for what purpose. The Employee Privacy Notice can be accessed here.

new_jobs.title: Parametric - Operations Analyst Cohort, Winter, 2027 (Recent Grads)
new_jobs.description:
Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, wealth management and investment management services.

About Parametric

Parametric is part of Morgan Stanley Investment Management, the asset management division of Morgan Stanley. We partner with advisors, institutions, and consultants to build portfolios focused on what's important to them and their clients. A leader in custom solutions for more than 30 years, we help investors access efficient market exposures, solve implementation challenges, and design multi-asset portfolios that respond to their evolving needs. We also offer systematic alpha and alternative strategies to complement clients' core holdings. Learn more here: https://www.parametricportfolio.com/about

This role is part of Parametric’ s hybrid working model, which includes working in the office 3 days a week and choosing to work remotely or in the office the remaining days of the week.

Excellent opportunity for recent or soon to be 2026 graduates! Office Locations: Seattle, Boston, Minneapolis, Alpharetta

WINTER COHORT STARTS - February, 2027

About The Operations Analyst Program

The Operations Analyst Program is an early-career development opportunity for driven recent and soon-to-be graduates who want to launch a career at the intersection of investment management, operations, data, and technology. Analysts use analytical, technical, and collaborative skills to help deliver operational excellence, solve business challenges, and improve outcomes for clients.

As investment operations evolve through data, automation, and AI, analysts gain hands-on experience supporting business-critical investment processes while helping identify opportunities to improve how work gets done. Through ownership of operational processes and exposure to continuous improvement, data analytics, automation, workflow design, and AI, analysts strengthen controls, improve decision-making, and contribute to scalable solutions that support clients and business growth.

Over three weeks, Analysts begin as a cohort with an immersion in Parametric's investment strategies, operating model, and Operations organization. Following onboarding, analysts join teams supporting Market, Client, or Control functions, where they develop domain expertise, learn business-critical workflows, and build an end-to-end understanding of how Operations supports clients, portfolios, risk management, and business growth.

Operations teams are responsible for the execution, oversight, servicing, and control activities that support the investment lifecycle. Analysts work closely with teammates and stakeholders across the organization to execute processes accurately, resolve operational challenges, improve controls, and deliver exceptional client outcomes.

In addition to their core team responsibilities, analysts may collaborate with specialized teams within Operations focused on process transformation, analytics, workflow modernization, automation, and AI-enabled solutions. Partnering with subject matter experts across Market, Client, and Control functions to identify opportunities, redesign processes, and implement scalable improvements that enhance operational effectiveness. Through this partnership, analysts may gain exposure to transformation initiatives while continuing to build deep operational expertise.

The program is designed for people who are curious about how businesses operate, motivated to improve processes, and eager to continue learning. As business needs evolve, analysts may gain exposure to different Operations functions, participate in cross-functional initiatives, or contribute to transformation efforts, broadening their knowledge, experience, and skill sets.

What You'll Do And Learn

Learn Parametric's investment strategies, operating model, and business-critical Operations workflows, and understand how Market, Client, and Control functions support clients, portfolios, risk management, and business growth.
Learn and execute business-critical investment operations workflows accurately and on time. Responsibilities may include activities such as cash and position reconciliation, trade lifecycle support, client servicing, corporate actions, account onboarding and maintenance, contracts, oversight activities, and billing, depending on team assignment.
Develop an end-to-end understanding of assigned processes, including activities, decisions, systems, data flows, controls, handoffs, and upstream and downstream dependencies.
Investigate exceptions, breaks, recurring operational issues, and client-impacting events using structured problem-solving and data analysis. Identify root causes, assess impacts, and recommend sustainable solutions.
Partner with Operations teams, portfolio managers, traders, sales, product management, technology teams, external providers, and other stakeholders to resolve issues, improve handoffs, and support business priorities.
Perform quality control and verification activities, maintain accurate records and documentation, and help ensure operational processes meet established policies, procedures, and control standards.
Analyze operational and investment data to identify patterns, anomalies, trends, bottlenecks, and emerging risks. Build reports, dashboards, or analytical tools that turn data into actionable insights and improvement opportunities.
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, or redesign workflows and contribute to process mapping, requirements gathering, testing, implementation, and adoption activities.
Collaborate with Automation, Reinvention & Collaboration (ARC) and other partners on process-improvement initiatives, workflow modernization efforts, analytics projects, automation solutions, and AI-enabled capabilities.
Use or learn tools such as Excel, Alteryx, Tableau, Power BI, SQL, Python, workflow automation platforms, process-modeling tools, and approved AI solutions, as appropriate to the assignment.
Contribute to operational excellence, analytics, automation, or process-improvement initiatives and present findings, recommendations, and outcomes to team members and business partners.

What You'll Bring

Associate or bachelor's degree completed by the program start date. Relevant fields may include industrial, process, or systems engineering; operations research; supply chain; data science or analytics; computer science; information systems; mathematics; statistics; finance; accounting; economics; or a related analytical, business, or technical field. Candidates from other majors with relevant quantitative, technical, or process-improvement experience are also encouraged to apply.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to break down ambiguous issues, work with data, identify root causes, and form well-supported conclusions.
A systems-thinking and continuous-improvement mindset, including curiosity about how people, processes, data, controls, and technology interact end to end and a desire to make work simpler, more accurate, efficient, scalable, and controlled.
High attention to detail and a commitment to quality, sound judgment, risk awareness, responsible use of data and technology, and positive client outcomes.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with teammates and stakeholders and communicate complex ideas in a clear and organized manner.
Ownership, learning agility, adaptability, and the ability to prioritize effectively in a collaborative, deadline-driven environment.
Experience using spreadsheets to organize and analyze information and communicate findings, or the ability to learn quickly.
Strong interest in building a career at the intersection of investment management, operations, process improvement, data, and technology.
Ability to work full-time (40 hours per week) by the program start date.

Preferred Qualifications

Coursework, internships, or project experience involving process mapping, continuous improvement, business analysis, data analysis, automation, workflow design, programming, analytics, or AI.
Exposure to one or more tools such as Alteryx, Tableau, Power BI, SQL, Python, workflow automation platforms, process-modeling tools, version control platforms, or similar technologies.
Familiarity with financial markets, investment management, or business operations. Prior investment operations experience is not required.
Experience contributing to a cross-functional project, presenting recommendations, developing a prototype, or helping others adopt a new process, workflow, or technology solution.

Salary & Benefits:
Set at $28.85 per hour ($60,000 annualized base)
, eligible annual bonus and for overtime. Cohort starts February, 2027!

The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary incentive compensation award. The successful candidate may be eligible to participate in the relevant business unit's incentive compensation plan, which also may include a discretionary bonus component. Morgan Stanley offers a full spectrum of benefits, including Medical, Prescription Drug, Dental, Vision, Health Savings Account, Dependent Day Care Savings Account, Life Insurance, Disability and Other Insurance Plans, Paid Time Off (including Sick Leave consistent with state and local law, Parental Leave and 20 Vacation Days annually), 10 Paid Holidays, 401(k), and Short/Long Term Disability, in addition to other special perks reserved for our employees. Please visit mybenefits.morganstanley.com to learn more about our benefit offerings.

Relocation assistance is not
provided for successful candidates.

Alpharetta Office: 1 Edison Drive Alpharetta, GA 30005

Boston Office: One Post Office Square, Floor 21 Boston, MA 02109

Seattle Office: 800 Fifth Avenue, Suite 2800 Seattle, WA 98104

Minneapolis Office: 3600 Minnesota Drive, Suite 200 Minneapolis, MN 55435

What You Can Expect From Morgan Stanley

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.

To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices into your browser.

new_jobs.title: Decision Intelligence Analyst
new_jobs.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Decision Intelligence Analyst – Corporate Engineering

At BNY, our culture allows us to run our company better and enables employees’ growth and success. As a leading global financial services company at the heart of the global financial system, we influence nearly 20% of the world’s investible assets. Every day, our teams harness cutting-edge AI and breakthrough technologies to collaborate with clients, driving transformative solutions that redefine industries and uplift communities worldwide.

Recognized as a top destination for innovators, BNY is where bold ideas meet advanced technology and exceptional talent. Together, we power the future of finance – and this is what is all about. Join us and be part of something extraordinary.

We’re seeking a future team member for the role of Decision Intelligence Analyst to join our Corporate Engineering team. This role is in Pittsburgh, PA or Lake Mary, FL.

In this role, you’ll make an impact in the following ways:

Provide decision intelligence and support to the Engineering Excellence Lead for Corporate Engineering by translating strategy into measurable execution outcomes.
Drive engineering excellence and delivery performance across Corporate Engineering Hubs and Corporate Activity Teams through adoption of standards, tooling, metrics, insights, training, communication, and governance.
Convert comprehensive engineering data—portfolio, headcount, financial, and execution signals—into clear insights and narratives for senior leaders.
Enable AI-accelerated workflows that automate insight generation while ensuring human judgment and context guide executive decisions.

To be successful in this role, we’re seeking the following:

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in analytics, engineering operations, finance, strategy, consulting, or related fields.
Approximately 2–4 years of relevant experience, ideally in analytics, engineering operations, finance, strategy, consulting, or rotational programs.
High learning agility and comfort working in ambiguous, fast-paced environments.
Strong skills in data synthesis, executive communication, and AI-enabled decision support.

At BNY, our culture speaks for itself, check out the latest BNY news at:

BNY Newsroom

Tes missions chez Mistplay : 

Mener des analyses proactives pour identifier des informations exploitables, notamment en se plongeant dans l'entonnoir du produit de base, les cohortes d'utilisateurs et en analysant les données relatives au comportement des utilisateurs, afin d'identifier les domaines de l'expérience utilisateur qui peuvent être améliorés pour générer de nouvelles opportunités d'affaires.

BA/BS en informatique, mathématiques, économie, statistiques ou autres domaines quantitatifs.

Familiarité avec Tableau ou tout autre outil de BI 

Familiarité avec les technologies de données en nuage telles que AWS, Azure ou Databricks pour interroger et construire des modèles de données et des rapports. 

Une attitude positive et une bonne dose de curiosité naturelle. Il faut répondre aux questions et nos données ne vont pas s'analyser toutes seules. (Nous y travaillons.)

Une passion pour les jeux et une bonne connaissance de l'industrie du jeu.

Senior Data Analyst I, Product

The Senior Data Analyst I, Product  within Mistplay's Data department will play a crucial role in enhancing Mistplay's business performance through insightful analysis and driving analytics strategy. Reporting to the Manager of Data Analytics & Experimentation, you will collaborate with Product & Lifecycle Managers to plan and analyze the results of A/B tests, and drive insights reporting in order to inform the release of new product features and engagement strategies.

What You'll Be Doing:

Conduct proactive analysis to identify actionable insights, including diving into the core product funnel, user cohorts, and analyzing user behaviour data, in order to identify areas of the user experience that can be improved to drive new business opportunities.

Define KPIs for the company and build automated dashboards, reports, and models to enable teams at Mistplay to make better decisions.

Design, orchestrate, and analyze the results of multivariate product experiments to help drive growth, improve existing product features, and test new areas of opportunity.

Collaborate with data, product, marketing, and engineering stakeholders to define business problems, scope out projects, identify risks and dependencies, and create execution plans.

BA/BS in Computer Science, Math, Economics, Statistics, or other quantitative fields

4+ years of work experience doing quantitative analysis (preferably in the tech industry) and a proven track record of impacting a business or product decisions

Pro-level ability to synthesize and communicate complex concepts and analyses in simple, easy-to-understand ways, to a wide range of technical and non-technical audiences

Past experience in A/B testing, and a strong foundational knowledge of core inferential statistics concepts (significance, power, confidence intervals, variance, etc.)

Fluency in SQL. Experience pulling highly dimensional and complex data, as well as modeling scenarios and sensitivity analysis using Excel

Experience with Python or another programming tool for statistical modeling

Familiarity with Tableau or any BI tool 

Familiarity with cloud data technologies such as AWS, Azure, or Databricks to query and build data models and reports 

Positive attitude and a healthy dose of natural curiosity. Questions have to be answered and our data isn't just going to analyze itself. (We're working on that.)

Bonus if you have:

A love of gaming and familiarity with the games industry

Understanding of data science and machine learning techniques

Experience working with very large data sets and distributed computing (Hive/Hadoop)

Role:

Superpower:

Project Orchestrator

Above The Fray is seeking a Project Manager, Client Delivery to join our Client Services team.
This is a hands-on, client-facing role responsible for keeping assigned digital commerce accounts organized, financially visible, clearly communicated, and moving forward.

The Project Manager serves as the operational counterpart to ATF’s technical and delivery leaders. While subject matter experts focus on strategy, solutions, and execution, this person maintains command of the project plan, budget, communication, decisions, commitments, and follow-through.

This is not a department leadership role. It is a working project management position for someone who enjoys being close to clients, teams, numbers, and day-to-day delivery.

Who You Are

You notice what needs to be done and act. You keep the right people informed, but you do not wait to be asked or use communication as a substitute for action.

You raise concerns early and constructively, focusing on solutions rather than blame. You treat feedback as useful information, give it respectfully, and receive it without defensiveness.

People trust you because you follow through. You do what you said you would do, when you said you would do it, and exceed the quality expected. When projects become pressured or unclear, you remain calm, direct, and easy to work alongside.

You are comfortable working in the details while maintaining awareness of the broader client relationship, financial position, and delivery objective.

What You Will Own

Client Delivery and Communication

You will be the day-to-day operational lead for assigned accounts. You will understand what the client is trying to accomplish, keep communication moving, and make sure conversations turn into clear decisions and action.
Serve as the primary operational contact for assigned clients.
Maintain awareness of client priorities, concerns, decisions, and commitments.
Respond promptly and ensure requests are acknowledged, assigned, and followed through.
Build trust through preparation, transparency, responsiveness, and consistency.
Participate in discovery sessions, planning meetings, business reviews, onsite engagements, and industry events as needed.
Communicate delivery risks, dependencies, budget constraints, and required tradeoffs clearly.

Project Operations and Financial Visibility

You will maintain an accurate view of how each project is performing and surface issues before they become emergencies.
Track project financials, working hours, burn rates, milestones, forecasts, and team capacity.
Monitor account staffing allocations and analyze how resource levels affect project budgets and delivery.
Flag budget overages, underutilization, time-tracking errors, forecast variances, and scope risks for team review.
Work with finance, operations, and delivery leaders to investigate discrepancies and prepare clear explanations.
Support prioritization, downscoping, and change-management discussions when requested work exceeds available budget.
Provide concise reporting on budget position, forecast, staffing impact, and emerging financial risks.

Planning, Coordination, and Follow-Through

You will create the structure that allows clients and delivery teams to move efficiently.
Own project plans, milestones, dependencies, action items, and delivery calendars.
Maintain the backlog and sprint board in close partnership with technical and client leads, ensuring work is prioritized, sufficiently defined, assigned, and ready to move forward.
Coordinate with Technical Architects, squad leads, engineers, designers, QA, marketing specialists, and other contributors.
Ensure teams have the information, access, approvals, and client input required to complete their work.
Organize planning sessions, demos, backlog reviews, and other delivery meetings appropriate to the account.
Ensure each meeting results in clear decisions, action items, owners, deadlines, and documented follow-through.
Surface blockers and unresolved decisions before they affect delivery.
Maintain the project’s decisions, risks, commitments, action items, and delivery status, coordinating with technical leads on technical documentation.
Maintain ticket hygiene by ensuring all work is assigned through properly written tickets with clear scope, description, and acceptance criteria.

What Success Looks Like

Clients receive timely, clear communication and understand what happens next.
Budgets, staffing concerns, scope risks, and delivery issues are surfaced early.
Project plans, boards, forecasts, action logs, and ownership remain current and reliable.
Meetings produce decisions and action rather than additional ambiguity.
Technical and delivery leaders can focus on their areas of expertise without repeatedly chasing administrative follow-up.
Assigned accounts become more organized, predictable, and financially healthy.
Clients and teammates view you as dependable, constructive, and easy to work with under pressure.

Qualifications

Approximately 3 to 5 years of project management, client delivery, account coordination, or related experience.
Experience in an agency, consultancy, software company, ecommerce business, or another client-service environment.
Experience coordinating digital, ecommerce, website, software, or technical projects.
Demonstrated responsibility for budgets, schedules, client communication, project reporting, or resource coordination.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to maintain awareness across several active accounts.
Comfort working with project financials, forecasts, staffing allocations, and delivery reporting.
Ability to turn conversations into clear decisions, actions, owners, and deadlines.
Strong client-facing written and verbal communication.
Ability to identify risks, gaps, and inconsistencies without waiting for someone else to raise them.
Experience working with distributed or international teams is helpful.
Familiarity with Jira, Confluence, Tempo, Slack, Google Workspace, and major ecommerce platforms is beneficial but not required.

Reporting Structure

Why Above The Fray?

We are driven by our simple, straightforward aim; Make it Better.
Ideal candidates will embrace and live this ethos in their everyday interactions and activity.
Work with the best. Every team member at ATF raises the bar for each other. A wide array of skill sets and talents, all at the top of their game. Expect to grow, and to promote the growth of others.

We really enjoy problem-solving together. As the climate allows, we regularly have team celebrations and company events. Happy hours, potlucks, company retreats, and international travel opportunities.

Be a part of something bigger than the sum of our parts. Being a contributing member of our community means we think beyond the confines of our business, and support the environment that props us up.

Company Description

A career here is life-enhancing.

At Syner-G, we enable our people to build careers that impact positively on their quality of life. Through our expertise, insight, consulting and management skills, we accelerate breakthrough science and delivery of life-enhancing therapies to more patients. We work across a diverse range of clients and projects, supporting many organizations from the most critical phases of the drug discovery and approval process through to commercialization. It is meaningful, varied and thought-provoking work with a strategic emphasis, a solutions-driven approach and significant, real-world outcomes, from science to delivery/success. To learn more about who we are and what drives us, watch our company video here
.

Underpinning this mission is a culture that aligns perfectly with what we want to achieve. We enable our people to grow, we support them in their learning and we reward them in so many different ways. In return, they play an instrumental role in maintaining our reputation across the globe as a strategic biopharma product development and delivery partner.

Syner-G was recently honored with BioSpace's prestigious "Best Places to Work" 2026 award, for the third consecutive year, along with many other award-winning programs to make a career here truly life-enhancing. These recognitions are a testament to our commitment to fostering a positive and engaging work environment for our employees, with a particular emphasis on culture, career growth and development opportunities, financial rewards, leadership and innovation.

At Syner-G, we recognize that our team members are our most valuable asset. Join us in shaping the future, where your talents are valued, and your contributions make a meaningful impact.

For more information, visit www.Synergbiopharma.com

Position Overview

Syner-G is seeking a Project Manager to oversee and manage construction and engineering projects from planning through commissioning and closeout. This role is responsible for coordinating project activities, maintaining schedules and budgets, and ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, and in alignment with quality and regulatory expectations. The Project Manager will work closely with clients, contractors, engineering teams, and internal stakeholders to drive successful project execution.

WORK LOCATION:

Travel to client sites may be required up to 100%, based on project demands and client expectations.

Key Responsibilities

(This list is not exhaustive and may be supplemented or adjusted as necessary.)

Keep the Project Director informed of project progress, risks, and issues, and provide recommended solutions or mitigation strategies.
Review technical submissions from Architectural and Engineering (A&E) firms, including MEP drawings, structural drawings, and construction specifications.
Respond to and manage construction communications such as RFIs, submittals, and technical clarifications.
Assist with preparation and execution of job start-up and close-out checklists.
Read, interpret, and manage project plans, specifications, contracts, subcontracts, purchase orders, correspondence, shop drawings, and other project-related documents.
Maintain accurate and complete as-built project documentation.
Support Transfer of Care and Custody (TOCC) to facilities operations and ensure proper documentation for transition from construction to maintenance mode.
Use project and construction management software such as ProCore, E-Builder, or Prolog.
Act as the owner’s representative on capital projects, ensuring alignment with client expectations and project goals.
Use Microsoft Project to develop, maintain, and track project schedules.
Participate in daily planning meetings, document observations, and ensure alignment across project teams.
Walk construction sites regularly to verify progress, identify field issues, and support resolution efforts.
Prepare daily reports, photo documentation, and progress measurements.
Review construction site safety documents such as work permits, task plans, and job hazard analyses, and collaborate with the client’s EHS team to ensure compliance.
Coordinate and support contractors including general contractors, construction managers, mechanical, electrical, and specialty trades.
Support project execution in active operating facilities, ensuring minimal disruption to ongoing operations.
Assist with start-up, commissioning, and handover of building systems including HVAC, emergency power, UPS systems, lab gases, RODI water, boilers, and steam generators.
Develop and implement document control, information management, and records governance processes.
Establish standards for filing structures, naming conventions, metadata, version control, and quality assurance.
Coordinate documentation requirements, deliverables, turnover strategies, and audit readiness across project teams.
Monitor compliance, documentation quality, and drive continuous process improvement.
Develop training materials, procedures, and best practices to ensure consistent adoption across the organization.

Qualifications And Requirements

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements below represent the education, experience, skills, knowledge, and abilities required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field preferred.
PMP certification is a plus.

Technical Experience

4–9 years of experience in project engineering or project management, preferably in industrial, chemical, petrochemical, biotech, or related environments.
Experience supporting or managing capital projects from design through construction and commissioning.
Experience coordinating contractors across multiple disciplines (GC, CM, mechanical, electrical, etc.).
Experience executing projects within active operating facilities.
Experience participating in commissioning and turnover of building systems such as HVAC, emergency power, UPS, lab gases, RODI water, boilers, and steam systems.
Experience conducting site walks, identifying field issues, and supporting resolution efforts.
Experience preparing daily reports, photo documentation, and progress tracking.
Experience reviewing safety documentation and collaborating with EHS teams.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong communication skills with the ability to interface effectively with client stakeholders, managers, contractors, and subcontractors.
Proficiency with Microsoft Project and familiarity with construction management software.
Detail-oriented with strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Essential Functions

Physical Demands :

The physical demands described here are representative of the requirements that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use a computer keyboard and mouse; reach with hands and arms; talk and listen. The employee is frequently required to walk and sit, as well as to lift and carry objects such as books and files weighing up to 25 pounds. The employee is occasionally required to stand, stoop, or kneel. Specific vision abilities required by this position include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, including moderate noise level, an indoor temperate environment, and light levels that are bright and conducive to minimal eye strain, typical for an office environment.

Total Rewards Program

We define total rewards as compensation, benefits, remote work/flexibility, development, recognition, and our culture with programs that support each of our reward pillars. This includes a market competitive base salary and annual incentive plan, robust benefit offerings, and ongoing recognition and career development opportunities. Employees also enjoy our generous flexible paid time off program, company-paid holidays, flexible working hours, and fully remote work options for most positions and the ability to work “almost anywhere.” However, if a physical work location is more for you, we have office locations in Greater Boston; San Diego, CA; Boulder, CO; and India.

Compensation

The expected salary range for this position is $120,000 to $130,000 yearly. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

Currently, Syner-G is unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, AI Infrastructure Capacity Planning
new_jobs.description:
About The Team

OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization builds and operates the infrastructure required to train and serve frontier AI models. The Capacity Planning team connects rapidly changing research and product demand with the compute, networking, storage, power, data center, hardware, and operational resources required to make that demand executable.

About The Role

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to build and lead capacity planning across OpenAI's large-scale AI infrastructure. You will translate uncertain workload demand into clear infrastructure requirements, allocation decisions, supply commitments, activation priorities, and long-range capacity strategies.

This role sits at the intersection of research, engineering, infrastructure, finance, sourcing, deployment, and operations. You will create the planning models, operating cadences, governance mechanisms, and source-of-truth systems that allow teams to understand what capacity is required, what is available, what is at risk, and what decisions must be made.

This is not a finance-only forecasting or reporting role. Success requires technical fluency across the infrastructure stack, strong analytical judgment, and the ability to move consequential decisions forward when requirements, timelines, and supply conditions change quickly.

Key Responsibilities

Own capacity-planning processes across near-term workload allocation, quarterly execution, and longer-range infrastructure horizons.
Translate research, training, inference, and product demand into compute, accelerator, cluster, networking, storage, rack, power, and site requirements.
Develop scenarios that make assumptions, confidence levels, constraints, sensitivities, and decision points explicit.
Reconcile requested demand against contracted, delivered, installed, activated, and workload-usable capacity.
Partner with research and engineering teams to understand workload priorities, technical dependencies, utilization patterns, and changing requirements.
Partner with sourcing, finance, hardware, deployment, and operations teams to align supply commitments, activation schedules, costs, and delivery risks.
Support allocation and prioritization decisions when infrastructure is constrained or delivery plans change.
Track infrastructure lead times, critical dependencies, utilization, headroom, forecast accuracy, activation readiness, and capacity risk.
Build dashboards, analytical tools, executive updates, and operating cadences that create a credible source of truth.
Drive mitigation plans for site delays, hardware shortages, network or storage constraints, workload changes, and other capacity risks.
Continuously improve planning models, governance, data quality, and accountability as OpenAI's infrastructure scales.

Qualifications

8+ years of experience in technical program management, infrastructure capacity planning, cloud infrastructure, supply planning, or a closely related field.
Demonstrated ownership of capacity planning for large-scale distributed systems, cloud platforms, AI or ML workloads, or hyperscale infrastructure.
Ability to translate ambiguous demand into structured assumptions, scenarios, technical resource requirements, and executable plans.
Technical fluency across compute, networking, storage, data center infrastructure, utilization, reliability, and deployment dependencies.
Strong analytical skills and experience developing planning models, operational metrics, dashboards, or data-driven decision systems.
Experience leading decisions across engineering, finance, sourcing, deployment, operations, and executive stakeholders.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain uncertainty, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly.

Preferred Skills

Experience planning GPU, accelerator, or AI infrastructure capacity for training or inference workloads.
Experience with cluster allocation, cloud capacity, hardware supply, infrastructure procurement, site readiness, or production activation.
Familiarity with forecasting methods, scenario planning, optimization, cost attribution, capacity economics, and utilization management.
Experience building planning tools or source-of-truth systems using SQL, Python, spreadsheets, BI platforms, or similar technologies.
Track record of improving utilization, reducing infrastructure cost or risk, and enabling critical workloads during periods of constrained supply.

Location

San Francisco, California. This role requires regular in-person collaboration with infrastructure, research, and operational partners.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.
